correctness.rationale: For simple unlabeled graphs with 1<=n<=6, the certificate's 2^(n choose 2)-mask enumeration and adjacent-transposition orbit closure cover every isomorphism class; Tarjan edge-block test correctly recognizes connected block graphs and globally interned 1-WL signatures compare against ALL graphs. Independently recomputing graph-atlas types and global colour refinements yielded all-graph counts (1,2,4,11,34,156), block-graph counts (1,1,2,4,9,22), exactly one ambiguous connected block graph (n=6) and 152 global 1-WL classes at n=6. G (two triangles joined by a bridge) and H (theta with paths 1,3,3) are nonisomorphic (2 versus 0 triangles), yet have the same equitable two-colour partition: two degree-3 nodes each see 1 degree-3 and 2 degree-2 neighbors and four degree-2 nodes each see one of each. Both have 7 edges. These direct checks give the explicit witness AND complete minimality/uniqueness to exactly n=6, without extrapolating to higher orders.

value.rationale: Global C²-identification is a natural and consequential graph-invariant boundary: the comparator includes every simple graph, so even a globally amenable block-graph family can develop its first failure. Exact six-vertex order, uniqueness among 22 connected block-graph types and a non-chordal comparator distinguish restricted-class enumeration from the unrestricted recognition problem. A complete sharp finite cutoff and fully determined mate class are a useful small obstruction benchmark; this is not claimed as a new general amenability theorem.
